Subject: RE: Production errors and timeouts impacting /generate — infra triage notes

Quick update from infra:

What we observed:
- At ~08:04–08:10 PDT there was a spike in concurrent KV-cache invalidations triggered by a rollout of a quantized-llama variant (internal rollout window). This caused temporary cache thrashing and increased per-request setup time on a subset of the us-west nodes.
- One autoscaler group experienced delayed scale-up due to a stuck termination on instance i-0a3b7 (GPU driver hung); this produced queueing and elevated p50/p95 latencies (p95 went from 240ms to ~3.4s).
- Error pattern: majority are timeouts (gateway timeout / 504) and transient inference exceptions. No signs of data corruption.

Immediate mitigations applied (08:20–08:55):
- Isolated the hung instance and drained traffic from that node.
- Disabled the quantized variant rollout (rollback started 08:25).
- Temporarily increased autoscaler aggression (shorter scale-up window) and kicked off new replacement instances.

Current status (09:02):
- Error rate has fallen from 12% -> ~2.1% over the last 20 minutes. Latency p95 trending down towards ~450–600ms.
- We’re still observing elevated tail latency under certain request sizes; investigation into kernel selection path and cache warmup is ongoing.

Next ETA: we expect stable p95/p99 in 45–60 minutes barring new incidents. I’ve opened INF-3421 for the detailed postmortem and follow-ups.

Jonas
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: latency-heatmap-0815-1015.png
